newsitem.title: UK: British soft drink firm to advertise on athletes' noses.
newsitem.headline: British soft drink firm to advertise on athletes' noses.

text.p: British advertisers have used toilet walls, eggs and even airline sick bags to promote their products, but now comes perhaps the most unusual ad space so far -- sportsmen's noses.
Soft drink company Britvic said Wednesday it will advertise its Red Card brand on nasal strips worn by Chelmsford City Football Club soccer players.

Nasal strips, traditionally clear plastic strips that adhere to the nose, are designed to improve breathing. They are becoming increasingly popular with soccer and rugby players and racing drivers, as well as other athletes.

Lucinda Semark, senior brand manager of Britvic soft drinks said: "We had the idea of branding nasal strips when we saw sprinter Linford Christie wearing Puma-branded contact lenses at the Atlanta Olympics last year."
Consumers anxious to wear their own Red Card nasal strip will be able to buy them from the soccer club. They will also be given away by Britvic as competition prizes.
Britvic is jointly owned by Bass Plc, Allied Domecq Plc, Whitbread Plc and PepsiCo Inc.
